title: VPC Handshake — Lightweight Playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight working playbook for the VPC handshake and minimal audit surface for customer-managed networking. Goal: give a simple, low-friction path for customers to onboard private deployments while preserving an immutable, queryable compact-audit trace that satisfies common compliance checks (SRE/infosec reviews, SOC-type evidence).

Context and motivation
- Many customers ask for an onramp that avoids heavy evidence bundles on day 0.
- We need something narrower than the full Attestation/Proof pipeline: lower bandwidth, small JSON payloads, minimal operator involvement.
- Target audience: mid-market/enterprise customers who self-manage VPC peering, NATs, and firewall rules, but rely on Redwood for control-plane attestations and event retention.

Success criteria (proposal)
- Onboard path that completes in < 30 minutes for standard network layouts.
- Compact audit entry for each approval/change that is verifiable (signed) and queryable within Console and via API.
- Retention policy defaults to 90 days for fastpath traces (configurable).
- Can escalate to full attested evidence flow when required by contract.

Design overview (high level)
1) Fasthandshake flow (recommended default)
  - Customer initiates VPC handshake from Console or API: provide VPC ID, CIDR hints, contact, and optional peering template.
  - Redwood control plane requests ephemeral proof token from customer connector (short-lived signed blob).
  - Control plane records a CompactAudit record and moves the change into PENDING_APPROVAL.
  - Operator or automated policy evaluates and either ACCEPT/REQUEST_MORE_INFO.
  - On ACCEPT: commit config, issue signed ChangeReceipt to both parties.

2) CompactAudit record (schema, human-readable form)
  - id: short stable id (e.g., rhd-20240225-6a3f)
  - ts: ISO8601 timestamp string
  - actor: human or service principal (user:alice@example.com, system:redwood-control)
  - op: one-line verb (vpc-peering:add, nat-router:update, egress-rule:add)
  - target: short resource path (cust/1234/vpc/us-east-1/vpc-0abcd)
  - evidence_ref: small list of URLs or object ids (can be empty for fastpath)
  - signature: base64 of signed digest (control-plane key)

  Example (single-line compact log entry):
  {"ts":"2024-02-25T14:22:03Z","id":"rhd-20240225-6a3f","actor":"user:sofia@redwood.ai","op":"vpc-peering:add","target":"cust/998/vpc/us-west-2/vpc-0a1b2c","evidence_ref":"s3://rwd-audit/998/2024-02-25/6a3f.json","signature":"sha256:ab12..."}

3) Approval gates and policy presets
  - Preset 0 (Fastpath): auto-approve changes that match a whitelist (CIDR within allowed set, non-overlapping peer). Creates CompactAudit only.
  - Preset 1 (Operator review): notify operator team, require manual acceptance within SLA window (2 hours).
  - Preset 2 (Attested Proof): full evidence bundle required (signed snapshots, traceroutes, operator smoke tests). Triggers the heavy attestation pipeline.

4) Escalation and rollback patterns
  - If PENDING_APPROVAL expires, auto-revert to LAST_KNOWN_GOOD and emit RevertAudit.
  - If post-commit telemetry shows connectivity regressions for 5 mins, system automatically opens a rollback ticket and flags the change for human triage.

Telemetry and sampling
- For the fastpath, we keep lightweight telemetry: request latency, decision time, and resulting status (accepted/auto-rejected/escalated).
- Sampling: full evidence uploads are only sampled for 1 in N fastpath changes (configurable per-customer, default N=500) to validate heuristics.

Retention & storage considerations
- CompactAudit entries stored in WAL-style append-only index for 90 days (default).
- Evidence blobs (when uploaded) are stored in customer-scoped buckets with lifecycle rules (default 365 days then archive).
- Users with enterprise retention can opt into longer retention and longer signing key lifetimes.

Console UX sketch (notes)
- Single "Start handshake" button in Private -> Networking -> Handshake. Minimal required fields.
- Small timeline card per change showing: compact id, ts, actor, op, gate (fastpath/operator/attested), state.
- "Download receipt" action to export signed JSON.

APIs (quick notes)
- POST /v1/private/vpcs/{cust}/handshake -> returns compact id and status (PENDING_APPROVAL)
- GET /v1/private/audit/{compact_id} -> returns CompactAudit JSON + signature
- POST /v1/private/vpcs/{cust}/handshake/ack -> operator ack endpoint

Security model
- Signatures use control-plane asymmetric keys (rotateable).
- Customer connector signs ephemeral proofs with customer key (if available) otherwise brokered HMAC token exchange.
- Least privilege: control plane only stores references to evidence; evidence objects encrypted at rest with per-customer KEK.

Open questions / risks (working list)
- What is the minimum legal acceptability of a CompactAudit entry for customers in regulated industries? (SLA/legal to answer)
- Edge-case: simultaneous updates to overlapping CIDRs from two actors — do we serialize or provide conflict resolution UI?
- Key rotation: how do we prove historical CompactAudit entries after control-plane key rotation? (store key version metadata)

Back-of-envelope implementation timeline (alpha)
- Week 0–2: implement CompactAudit schema, append-only store, basic Console UX.
- Week 3–4: implement fasthandshake POST flow + auto-approve whitelist policy.
- Week 5–6: operator review queue and ack endpoint + sample signed receipts.

Next steps / immediate TODOs
- [ ] Sync with Legal on evidence minimization for fastpath (Aisha)
- [ ] Write API contract for handshake endpoints (Marcus)
- [ ] Spike lightweight signature key versioning and signing proof (Liam)
- [ ] Add console mock to design board and run 1 customer pilot

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally small-scope: we want a pragmatic default that avoids scaring customers off with heavy attestation up-front.
- If a customer requires the full forensic bundle, the flow should seamlessly escalate into our existing attestation pipeline (reuse components).
